misses.answer: Not necessarily. The standard default of 1,000 concurrent executions per Region is documented, but AWS also says new accounts start with reduced concurrency quotas. The Lambda scaling page says that always your account has a total concurrency limit of 1,000 concurrent executions across all functions in a Region. However, the Lambda quotas page and the AWS Lambda endpoints and quotas page both state that new AWS accounts have reduced concurrency and memory quotas, and that AWS raises these automatically based on your usage. The docs I could reach do not give the specific reduced number for a new account. To see the value that applies to your account, check the Service Quotas console for Lambda, or run aws lambda get-account-settings. You can also request an increase.

misses.answer: No, you can't switch the type. The workflow type can't be updated after you create a state machine, so an Express workflow stays Express. To get 90 days of history, either (1) create a new Standard state machine with the same definition and role and point callers at it, since Standard workflows let you retrieve full execution history via the Step Functions API for up to 90 days after an execution completes; or (2) keep the Express workflow, enable logging to CloudWatch Logs, and set the log group's retention to at least 90 days, because always log data is kept indefinitely but can be configured. I did not confirm the exact Express history retention behavior or the logging setup steps in the docs, so verify those before relying on option 2.
